description: The frontend's Skill surface: what discovery may render about a skill, and what it must never become. A Skill is procedural knowledge (how) - not a capability (what) and not an agent (who). This catalog ships EMPTY on purpose: `ai.skill` has no contract-lock row, the backend declaration carries `versioning: publicationPending`, and a frontend that listed skills anyway would be inventing both the skills and the contract that defines them. What the UI renders in that state is the canonical unsupported answer.

publicationPending.what: manifest/ai-lego-set.json declares ai.skill (the Skill LEGO, status `planned`) with its lifecycle, operations, operation permissions and disclosure levels, but no contract-lock row publishes ai.skill and the declaration itself says `versioning: publicationPending`, so the frontend has no contract version to bind to

rules: Discovery only: listing, search, filter and detail read declarations. Nothing here selects, loads or executes a skill.
The six lifecycle states are six facts. No boolean `enabled` is derived from them, and none of them is an execution state.
A skill carries neither a permission nor an authority: the declared operation permissions are requirements of a backend operation, never a grant the UI holds.
With `ai.skill` unpublished the canonical unsupported state is rendered: no fallback capability, no execution control and no tool list.
Skill entries are supplied to the runtime by the application (or declared here once a contract exists); this package never reads the backend tree.

A declaration that moved past the quoted vocabulary is reported (`declarationDrift`, XA-19) and never adopted silently; a version claimed in a file is reported as `declaredVersion` and is still not a publication.

alignment.rule: A declaration handed over by the application is compared with the words this package quotes; a difference is reported as data (`declarationDrift`) with both spellings and the owner, and is never resolved by adopting a word this package cannot quote.
